capabilities.description: Store a model in the vault with encryption. Declares: mutates.

capabilities.name: vault.get
capabilities.description: Retrieve and decrypt a model from the vault. Declares: decrypts.

capabilities.name: vault.list

capabilities.name: utility.export

capabilities.name: utility.cache
capabilities.description: Show cache statistics. Declares: no effects.

capabilities.name: conversion.convert

capabilities.name: conversion.list-conversions

note: requires_grant is now DERIVED. An earlier version of this file said the opposite -- that IronVault declared no effect data and both fields were judgement -- and that was true when it was written. The tool now declares mutates, decrypts and network per command, so requires_grant is true where any of the three holds, and this manifest reads them rather than guessing. The field that carries the weight is `decrypts`, and it exists because a mutation flag alone would have been actively misleading here: get, export, archive, convert, analyze and deduplicate change nothing in the vault and are precisely the commands that produce plaintext. An agent gated on mutation would have treated all six as harmless reads. Budgets remain judged, and mark the commands that move or transform whole models. Two things the schema is honest about. cloud is the only command declaring all three effects, since it pushes and pulls models off the machine. And `serve` does not appear here because it is not in this build -- the schema reflects what was compiled, not what the source can offer, which is the correct behaviour for a discovery document but means a caller must read the ontology from the binary it is actually talking to.
